37 stations (lines 542-592), 25 of them starred. Both counts match the lead-in ("thirty-seven lighthouses and lightvessels ... Twenty-five stations have sent in returns, and twelve have failed"). The character is left out for exactly the six stations the other reader listed.

CORRECTION: the Dungeness Point row (line 592) wrongly has type "Lighthouse". The print reads just "Dungeness Point; white, fixed.", so type should be null. Please fix this before loading the data. Flamborough Head (line 551) is entered correctly with type null.

How I split the fields:
- Fragments are each printed line with only the left indentation removed. The * and all punctuation are kept.
- In name, type and place I dropped the commas, semicolons and full stops that separate fields (e.g. "Berwick." gives name "Berwick"). The fragments keep them.
- Characters that run onto a second line are joined with one space.
- coast is the section heading you gave (EAST COAST OF ENGLAND). There are no sub-headings inside this list.
- The "Lightvessel" and "Lighthouse" types are written out in full in this list, not abbreviated as L.V./L.H.

Rows to check:
- Whitby (550): I took "High Light" as part of the name ("Whitby, High Light"), like "Hoy Sound (Low)". Only the High Light is listed.
- Teesmouth (549): "No. 5 Buoy" is in place and "Lightvessel" in type. The printed text runs "Teesmouth, No. 5 Buoy Lightvessel", with no comma before Lightvessel.
- Farn Islands (545): "(two lights)" is in other. It is a separate row from Longstone (543), which is described as "on the most easterly of the Farn Islands".
- Spurn Point (553, no character, not starred) and Spurn Lightvessel (554, starred) are separate stations.
- Hunstanton (565) uses a comma before the character ("Lighthouse, white, fixed"); the other rows use a semicolon.

Copied as printed, probably errors:
- "while, fixed" (Whitby) means "white".
- "red fight, fixed" (Lowestoft) means "red light".
These may be typesetting or Gutenberg transcription slips; it's worth checking them against the scan.

Spellings of the time, kept as printed: "Farn" (Farne), "Hasborough" (Happisburgh), "Languard Point" (Landguard), "Orfordness", "Newarp", "Gull-stream", "East-side", "South-sand Head", "Souter Point".
